lessons.title: How Offer Engineering works
body: Offer Engineering is the first practical system in the DigitalOps CREATE library. It exists to help you turn knowledge, professional experience, or a practical skill into a clearly positioned digital product offer — not a vague idea, a finished document you could hand to a customer.

Rather than starting with a product format, you'll work through eight short modules that build on each other: understanding the market, mapping the real problems, designing an outcome worth wanting, structuring the offer, pricing it, naming it, and preparing a validation test. Each module ends with a short exercise and a ready-to-use AI prompt, and every answer you give feeds the next module — you're never asked to repeat yourself.
By the end, all nine pieces compile automatically into your Offer Blueprint — a single, polished, exportable document. That's the actual product: not the lessons, the finished Blueprint.
lessons.insight: This sequence can't be reordered — each module needs the output of the one before it. Resist the urge to jump to pricing or naming early; a name or price with nothing behind it is the most common reason a first offer doesn't sell.

exercise.instructions: One question sets your starting context. It doesn't skip you past any module — everyone completes M1–7 in full.
exercise.question: Where are you starting from?

options.label: I'm starting from a skill or expertise — I don't have an offer yet
options.hint: You'll build your Target Customer Profile and Problem Inventory from scratch in M1 and M2.

options.label: I already sell something, but it was never built this rigorously
options.hint: You'll use your current offer as the starting material in M1 and M2, re-examining who it's really for and what problems it actually solves.
